newsitem.title: USA: Brent rises in late US trade; foreign crudes slow.
newsitem.headline: Brent rises in late US trade; foreign crudes slow.

text.p: North Sea Brent rose is late U.S. trading Monday, with two full boats changing hands, traders said.
Two boats of paper March Brent moved at $22.64 and $22.65 a barrel, up 10-11 cents from the IPE close of $22.54 in London.
Three partial March Brents traded at $22.60, $22.61 and $22.62 a barrel.
March/April Brent was dealt twice at 43 cents, down one cent from the London settlement.

Meanwhile, foreign crudes are moving into the U.S. Gulf Coast at a slow pace, mainly because of various refinery turnarounds, chronically poor margins and volatility in the spread between West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and Brent, refiners said.
The March spread was around $1.55-60 a barrel Monday afternoon, down five cents from late Friday in a gradual narrowing trend.
Although the transatlantic arbitrage remains open, the economic incentive for sellers has diminished, traders said.
"The margins aren't too terrific, so there's no reason to be in a hurry," said one refiner, commenting on the slow pace of transatlantic trade.
Brent is on offer to the Gulf Coast around 30-35 cents under March WTI/Cushing for March 15-20 delivery, traders said.
On the Latin American front, Uruguay's state-owned oil refiner ANCAP is seeking one million barrels of crude for delivery April 5-10 to the Jose Ignacio terminal, trade sources said.
ANCAP had temporarily suspended its regular crude tenders during the planned shutdown of the 34,600 barrels per day (bpd) La Teja refinery.
The facility is due back on line around the end of February, sources said.
The tender will be awarded on Wednesday, February 5.
